recipes.name: Slow Cooker Mongolian Beef
ingredients_raw: 1 pound flank steak, cut into bite-size pieces
3 large green onions, sliced diagonally into 1/2 inch pieces

steps.text: Place flank steak and cornstarch into a resealable plastic bag. Shake the bag to evenly coat the flank steak with the cornstarch. Allow to steak rest for 10 minutes.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir steak until evenly browned, 2 to 4 minutes. Place onion, garlic, flank steak, green onions, soy sauce, water, brown sugar, ginger, and hoisin sauce in a slow cooker. Cook on Low setting for about 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Mongolian Beef
raw_recipe.description: This Chinese restaurant favorite is made with tender chunks of flank steak, onion, garlic, soy sauce, and hoisin sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was very good. I used round steak that I had on hand and it worked fine. I didn't have any hoisin sauce so I made some. There's not a recipe on this site so here's the recipe for hoisin. 4 Tbsp Soy sauce, 2 Tbsp Peanut butter,1 Tbsp Honey/molasses,2 tsp White vinegar,1/8 tsp Garlic powder, 2 tsp Sesame seed oil, 20 drops Chinese-style hot sauce, 1/8 tsp Pepper. My family said "it's a keeper!

this was AWESOME!! word to the wise, its quite sweet, so if you dont like sweet, cut back on the sugar. we loved it!! flank steak was too expensive, so i substituted flap meat and it was so tender.served it over white rice. i also added chili garlic sauce to kick up the heat, maybe 2-3 Tbsp. loved the flavor combo spicy/sweet. thanks for a ridiculously easy and delicious recipe!!!

I used a 2 1/2 lb flank steak so I doubled the sauce, which was probably not necessary since there was so much in the end. I only added half the brown sugar called for and it was still very sweet. I also added a couple of tablespoons of asian chili sauce to give it some heat and saved the green onions until it was almost done. I thought it was excellent! Served with white rice and green beans.

This had a very good taste. I used a choice grade chuck roast that weight about two pounds so doubled the ingredients. I did omit the sugar and also cooked the House Fried Rice to serve it over. We enjoyed it and I plan on making it again in the future. I was hesitant to do a Chinese dish in a slow cooker versus my Wok but it turned out fine. Okay after making this for the third time now 7 hours is too long of a cooking time on low. Onions were mush. Third time I did add some broccoli and a third of a Leek. The Leek imparted a very nice flavor to this dish. I think I will add the onions at a later time and reduce my cooking time. We both still loved it and will be making again soon.

Chinese style not a fav at home so I changed it. Added cut carrots and sliced mushrooms toward end. Used pork tenderloin cut in 3 chunks so it could be arranged in slices showing meat's color edged in browned sear. Served slices over noodles, topped with veggies and sauce and with separately cooked green veggi+e (whole green beans first, brocolli second night), Fork tender. He loved it. Will make again.

Great flavor ! I didn't find the need to grill the beef before putting in cooker for 4 hours. I also added in yellow and red bell pepper for color and served over spaghetti squash. Tasted great ! Will make again.

I love this recipe ! I buy our meta in bulk, so I use beef chuck stew meat and cook on low for 7 hours - so tender and delicious! I also try not to use refined sugar whenever possible, so I use 1/3 cup of honey instead - plenty sweet for the kiddo! I also saw other recipes that add carrots, so I ad 1 cup of diced carrot with the onion for a little extra nutrition.

I made this as written, except I only used 1/4 cup of brown sugar because of all the comments saying it was too sweet. Definitely still too sweet for my tastes. This definitely doesn't taste like what I get at my local Chinese restaurants, but I appreciated the ease of the recipe. I'd probably only use 1-2 Tbsp sugar next time, and use less hoisin sauce as the flavor was overpowering. The meat also fell apart into crumbles, so this could probably benefit from less time in the slow cooker. The boyfriend did say he liked it, but found it "a little sweet". He added Sriracha to his. I also agree with the others who said adding the onions in later so they don't get mushy. In terms of it being too salt, I used low sodium soy sauce, which was fine.

I tripled this recipe for family and friends and everybody LOVED it.....just loved it. I served it with steamed rice, a red wine vinegar based slaw, sparkling water and beer, and an orange sherbet with plain wafers for dessert. It was a hit. Even my young friend (in college), who doesn't cook, asked for the recipe. I added some sliced water chestnuts to the mix for crunch and interest, stirred in the sliced green onions toward the end of the cooking time, and cut my onion slices a little larger to ensure they could be "seen" on the plate. My Ukranian friend couldn't eat enough of it....I'll definitely make this again.

I made this using my Instant Pot. After browning the meat, I cooked it with high pressure for 13 minutes and 15 minutes NPR. I used half the amount of sugar and thought it was still very sweet. It makes a ton of sauce! Next time I'll either double the meat or cut the sauce in half. Very good, easy recipe!

This was my first time buying flank steak, and i think it's a very good meat cut for this recipe. I did not find this recipe to be too salty nor toow sweet, however, i did use 1.5 cups of water instead of just 1/2 cup. I also did not slow cook, i made it on the stove top and let it simmer on low for about 30 minutes. I think if i had simmered it for another 30 minutes, the steak would ahve been perfectly tenderized, but not mushy. My boyfriend was a little bit indifferent about the recipe, but i quite liked it. I added mushrooms and a few dashes of cayenne pepper.

Everything about this recipe works. I can't get flank steak here, but thinly sliced bottom round worked and it still got raves. The flavors are well-balanced and the instructions are straightforward. Kudos 👏

This was very good. I made my own hoisin sauce, using the Allrecipes recipe, which I think added some good flavor. Served over brown rice with steamed broccoli. This is going into the meal prep rotation.
Great flavor! Added sliced mushrooms. Mmmm!
Made this so many times A family staple!
lemon grass and sino herbs 5-spice, cinnamon, and paprika, lime or lemon zest
Very tasty. Added red pepper for spice
Was a tad but sweet but the rest of the family loves it definitely doing this again think it's going to be a family favourite
This was almost perfect. It was way too sweet for me. Kids loved it (naturally!). But I will try again, but with less sugar added.

I had sirloin steak on hand so that is what i used. After reading the reviews i decided that only some of the people suggested reducing the sugar, so i kept it to the recipe and personally thought it was wonderful. No need to reduce the sugar in my opinion. It was a big hit in my house of 6. Easy and fully of flavor, this will be a repeat recipe !
